claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by competition between FCC and BCC phase formation.
Atomic-size difference influences the competition between FCC and BCC phase formation.
Valence-electron concentration influences the competition between FCC and BCC phase formation.
The proposed material state is as-cast or annealed Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy.
In situ high-pressure synchrotron X-ray diffraction will be used to study phase transformations.
The proposed experiments extend to temperatures of 1000°C.
The proposed experiments extend to pressures of 10 GPa.
FCC and BCC phase formation determines alloy phase stability.
Changes in FCC and BCC phase formation affect the resulting alloy properties.
The proposed comparison will produce a 20% increase in high-temperature yield strength relative to the baseline alloy.
The proposed comparison will produce a 30% improvement in environmental resistance, assessed through corrosion rate, relative to the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy is Al0.1Co0.1Cr0.2Fe0.3Ni0.3, corresponding to Al10Co10Cr20Fe30Ni30 in atomic percent.
The hypothesis is claimed to apply within the stated composition ranges: Al 0.05–0.2, Co 0.05–0.2, Cr 0.1–0.3, Fe 0.2–0.4, and Ni 0.2–0.4.
Grain size and defects may also influence the relationship between composition descriptors and phase stability.
The falsification experiment will measure phase fraction, lattice parameter, and yield strength across varying compositions.
The hypothesis will be falsified if phase stability has a correlation coefficient below 0.5 with atomic-size difference and valence-electron concentration.
